body.body:
## What

Make shared test-fixture teardown terminate and wait for harness doubles and their descendants, with PID-based regression coverage. CI now fails and reruns tests that leak output handles; the leak-detection regression also waits for its own deliberately leaked processes to exit.

Raise the cross-platform gate’s timeout to 180 minutes and its job’s to 220 minutes. Give the readjust store journey 600 seconds and other Windows tests 540 seconds to accommodate the slower runner image; other platforms retain their existing limits. Prevent the maintenance failure fixture from repeating its command during the same phase on slow hosts.

## Why

Leftover processes keep the required Windows check’s output open after tests pass, forcing two-hour reruns and blocking correct changes. This repeatedly blocked #904’s fix for 30–50 GB of daily Codex plugin catalog downloads. Cleanup lets the check finish when its work ends; the increased limits give the existing test tiers time to complete.

## Additional info

Windows containment includes orphaned descendants. Unix cleanup covers processes still descended from the test at teardown and continues waiting for those it finds even if their parents exit; processes orphaned to init before teardown remain outside that guarantee.

The macOS regression assertion failed because a Linux-only `/proc` probe treated exited zombies as running. The probe now uses `ps`, and teardown accepts macOS’s unclassified `?` process states.

The leak-detection regression previously passed on Linux but was itself marked `LEAK-FAIL` on Windows because its inner runs’ sleepers inherited the outer test’s output handles. It now waits for their recorded PIDs to exit and asserts that none remain on every supported platform.

## What

Adopt onetaskgraph 0.7.0 across the linked store family and matching CLI, bringing producer-side project and document caching. Extend the existing engine integration journey to compare project-read results and requests with caching enabled and disabled, retaining its write-back and recovery coverage.

## Why

Managers need the same fresh, quota-saving store behavior in dispatched graph work and the read API as in standalone board reads.

## Additional info

Breaking dependency update: public plan/store types expose the producer’s changed Project, Document, and VersionCoverage surface. Existing gh2 task versions require another read after the move to gh3. Engine reads remain unpinned and versions remain opaque; no engine-side cache or token translation is added.
